title: Soil Health Card Scheme & Soil Health Management Norms
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India
content: The Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme promotes Soil Test-Based Nutrient Management (STBNM) to address declining fertilizer response ratios. Frequency: Soil Health Cards are issued to farmers every 2 years for their specific land holdings. Reported parameters: Card reports status on 12 parameters: 1. Macro-nutrients (N, P, K), 2. Secondary nutrients (S), 3. Micronutrients (Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, Bo), and 4. Physical parameters (pH, Electrical Conductivity, Organic Carbon). Card deliverables: Specific fertilizer and manure dosage recommendations customized for 6 selected crops grown by the farmer, including soil amendment advice (lime for acidic soils, gypsum for alkali soils). Benefits: Helps farmers reduce indiscriminate use of urea, saves 15-20% fertilizer expenses, and prevents secondary micronutrient deficiencies. How to obtain: Soil samples collected by State Agriculture Department extension officers or village level entrepreneurs. Farmers can download their cards using Aadhaar or Mobile number on the national portal https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in.
